dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.text: Welcome to the WKU Technology Workshop. This is where students learn how products are designed and manufactured. Shall we begin?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Yes, please. I've been looking forward to this.

dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.text: So — we start here, at the design station. All products are first designed on a computer. The specifications are drawn up by engineering students.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: Are the designs shared with the rest of the team?

dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.text: Yes — they're uploaded to a shared system. Then they're reviewed by supervisors. If they're approved, the model is sent to the printer.

dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.text: Exactly. The prototype is printed here. Then it's tested — stress tests, weight tests, heat tests. If it fails, the design is modified and printed again.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: How long is the prototype stage?

dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.text: It varies. Sometimes a design is approved on the first attempt. Often it's revised three or four times before it's accepted.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: And what happens after it's accepted?

dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.text: The final design is transferred to this workstation. The materials are sourced — we use local suppliers when possible. Then the product is assembled here, by students.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: So it's assembled by hand, not by machine?

dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.text: In this workshop, yes. In real industry, most steps are automated — things are done by robots or machines. But here we want students to understand every stage by doing it themselves.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: And then the finished product is inspected?

dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.text: Correct. It's inspected by a supervisor, then photographed and stored in our showcase. The best ones are displayed at the end-of-year exhibition.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: Has any student project ever been used commercially?

dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.text: One was adapted and used by a local company last year. It's quite rare — but it happens.

questions.text: "The specifications are drawn up by engineering students." This is:
questions.hint: "are drawn up" = passive present simple (am/is/are + past participle). The engineering students = the agent (by...).

questions.text: "The prototype is printed here." What is the agent?
questions.hint: The agent (who/what does it) is the 3D printer, but it's not stated. Common in process descriptions!

questions.text: "The design is modified." — Active voice equivalent:
questions.hint: "The design IS MODIFIED." (passive) → "They MODIFY the design." (active). ✅

questions.text: "One design was adapted ___ a local company."
questions.hint: Agent in passive sentences = "BY". "Was adapted BY a local company." ✅
"is approved" = passive (is + past participle). "Approved" = past participle of "approve".

questions.text: "The products are displayed." — Past passive becomes:
questions.hint: Present passive: "are displayed" → Past passive: "WERE displayed." ✅
"Materials ARE SOURCED from local suppliers." = passive present simple. ✅

questions.text: "In real industry, most steps are automated." "Automated" means:
opts: Done by machines without human involvement
questions.correct: Done by machines without human involvement
questions.hint: "automated" = done automatically by machines, not by people.
